title: The Third Voyage of Sindbad (मराठी)
summary: Sindbad recounted the perilous third voyage: [MR]
full_text:
Sindbad recounted the perilous third voyage:

'Once more the desire for adventure drove me to the seas. While sailing near the Isle of Zughb, a terrifying storm drove our vessel onto the Mountain of Apes. Thousands of fierce, diminutive apes swarmed our ship, gnawed through the rigging, cast the crew ashore, and sailed away with our vessel.

Stranded on the island, we explored the rocky interior and discovered a colossal fortress built of black stone, with double gates of ebony. Entering the vast hall, we found it furnished with iron spits as long as spears and heaps of human bones.

At sunset, the earth shook, and an enormous Giant entered: he was tall as a palm tree, with eyes like glowing coals, ears like an elephant, and teeth like curved tusks!

The monster seized our companions one by one, intending to devour us. Realizing that passive waiting meant certain death, I rallied the surviving crew: 'Brothers! Let us not perish like sheep; let us use the iron spits to blind the beast while he sleeps, and build rafts of driftwood on the beach!'

When the giant fell into a thunderous slumber, we heated two colossal iron spits in the hearth until they glowed red, and with united strength, thrust them simultaneously into the monster’s eyes!

The blinded giant roared with terrifying fury, groping in the dark as we fled to the beach. We pushed our wooden rafts into the surf and pulled with our oars. Though the giant’s companions hurled boulders into the sea, shattering two of our rafts, I and two companions escaped into the open waves.

After surviving a giant sea-serpent on a neighboring shore, a passing merchant vessel picked me up and carried me to the port of Basra, where my steadfast courage once again brought me back in safety to Baghdad.'
moral: United teamwork, courageous strategy, and persistence overcome the most terrifying monsters. [MR]
